summary: Iteration 2 — backend-focused regression on the new athlete `competition_ids` feature + dashboard contract. Ran the full pytest suite (29 tests total, 7 new for this iteration) against EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Initial run uncovered 1 CRITICAL bug (POST /api/athletes 500 when client omits `competition_ids`). Applied a one-line fix in /app/backend/server.py::create_athlete (filter None before splat into strict Athlete model). After fix, 29/29 pass (100%). Verified competition_ids round-trips through POST + PATCH + GET; verified PATCH with empty list [] is accepted (not filtered as None); verified other-field PATCH does not clobber competition_ids; verified user-scoping still enforced (User B → 404 on User A's athlete). Verified GET /api/dashboard returns all 10 fields needed by the new top stat tiles + bottom 3-column compact stat row (outstanding_balance, unpaid_expense_balance, booking_balance, month_spend, total_payments_ytd, athletes_count, total_raised, competitions_count, total_expenses_ytd, next_competition). Frontend smoke test was NOT performed (scope: backend-first). Deprecated shadow* warnings still emitted in expo logs by some upstream/third-party component(s) — theme.ts is fixed but warnings persist (low priority, see action items).

minor.issue: Carry-over from prior iter: no input validation that competition_ids[] strings actually reference real Competition rows for the user. Currently any string accepted. Not breaking but allows orphan references. Consider validating via $in lookup or accept-as-is and treat UI as source of truth.
Same as above — competition_ids strings are not validated against existing competitions; cross-user comp IDs could be persisted on an athlete (though never resolved by other queries). Low risk.

All PATCH endpoints filter `None` values via `{k:v for k,v in dump().items() if v is not None}`. This means clients cannot explicitly null-out an optional field (e.g. clear `notes`, `booking_link`, `due_date`). Acceptable for now but worth noting — use exclude_unset semantics if explicit clears become needed.

react_native_issues.issue: Despite /app/frontend/src/theme.ts migrating to `boxShadow` string, expo logs still show repeated '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' warnings. Likely originate from a third-party RN component (e.g. react-native-paper, react-native-elements, or @react-navigation drawer/elements) still using shadowColor/shadowOffset. Reference: /var/log/supervisor/expo.err.log. Low priority — does not affect functionality. Recommend grepping node_modules-using callsites: `grep -rn 'shadowColor\|shadowOffset\|shadowOpacity\|shadowRadius' /app/frontend/app /app/frontend/components /app/frontend/src 2>/dev/null` and (if all clean) upgrading the offending third-party lib.

action_items: (Done by tester) Fixed CRITICAL 500 in POST /api/athletes when `competition_ids` not supplied — filter None from model_dump() before splatting into strict Athlete(...). See server.py::create_athlete. Pre-existing mobile create-athlete UI was about to break with this iteration's new field (any client that doesn't send competition_ids → 500).
(Optional) Validate `competition_ids` entries on POST/PATCH /api/athletes refer to real Competition rows owned by current_user. Currently any string accepted.

(Optional) The CompetitionUpdate / BookingUpdate / PATCH filter pattern `{k:v ... if v is not None}` blocks explicit field-clears. Consider exclude_unset semantics if UI ever needs to clear a field to null.
(Optional / low priority) Investigate residual 'shadow* deprecated' warnings in expo logs — likely from a third-party RN component still using shadowColor etc. theme.ts itself is correct now.
(Carry-over from iter 1) Set JWT_SECRET >= 32 chars in backend/.env; pin bcrypt<4.1 or upgrade passlib; (optional) HTTPBearer(auto_error=False) for consistent 401 on missing token.
critical_code_review_comments: ROOT CAUSE of the create-athlete 500: `AthleteCreate.competition_ids: Optional[List[str]] = None` was added, but in the endpoint `Athlete(**payload.model_dump())` passes `competition_ids=None` to the strict `Athlete` model whose field is `List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)`. Pydantic v2 rejects None for non-Optional list → 500. Pattern smell: anywhere a non-strict Create model splats into a strict storage model, None-tolerant filtering is required. Same pattern is used elsewhere in server.py (e.g. fundraisers, payments) and is currently safe only because those Create models have hard defaults rather than Optional.
PATCH /api/athletes correctly accepts `competition_ids: []` because the filter `if v is not None` keeps empty list (verified by test_patch_athlete_empty_competition_ids_accepted).
Dashboard endpoint contract is unchanged and fully backward-compatible — all 10 fields the new dashboard tiles consume are present and numeric (verified by TestDashboardBalanceFields).

server.py is still a single 1088-line file (>700 guideline). Recommend splitting into routers/ subpackage as feature surface grows (auth, athletes, expenses, payments, competitions, bookings, fundraisers, dashboard, reminders, imports).

rca_of_issue: Bug: POST /api/athletes returned 500 whenever the request body omitted `competition_ids`. Repro: `curl -X POST $API/athletes -H 'Auth: Bearer …' -d '{"name":"X"}'` → 500. RCA: New `AthleteCreate.competition_ids: Optional[List[str]] = None` produced `payload.model_dump() = {..., 'competition_ids': None}`. The endpoint then did `Athlete(**dump)` which feeds None to `Athlete.competition_ids: List[str]` (no Optional, no None allowed) — Pydantic v2 raised ValidationError → FastAPI mapped to 500. Mitigation applied: in `create_athlete`, build `data = {k:v for k,v in payload.model_dump().items() if v is not None}` before splatting, allowing the strict Athlete model's `default_factory=list` to kick in. Re-tested with 29/29 pass.
